figure.name: Friedrich Hayek
figure.role: Economist and political theorist focused on prices, knowledge, markets, planning, and liberal institutions.
figure.hook: Hayek = prices, knowledge, and the planning problem.
whyHere: Hayek belongs here because the project needs the strongest market-side argument, not a straw man.
He matters because debates over socialism, planning, and markets often turn on how much knowledge any central authority can actually collect and use.
figure.cleanIdea: Markets can coordinate dispersed information through prices, while centralized planning faces a knowledge problem.

sources.title: Hayek / The Use of Knowledge in Society
sources.note: Source lead for dispersed knowledge and price signals.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Hayek: prices, knowledge, markets, planning, liberalism, and what central planners can or cannot know.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The market-road argument says prices can coordinate dispersed information that planners cannot easily gather.

ideas.title: Knowledge Problem
ideas.plainDefinition: The knowledge problem is the claim that economic knowledge is dispersed across people, places, needs, and timing.
ideas.context: In the Hayek path, planning is limited because no central office can easily hold all the local information prices summarize.
ideas.whyMatters: The knowledge problem matters because it is one of the serious arguments against centralized economic planning.

sources.title: Hayek / The Use of Knowledge in Society

ideas.title: Price Signals
ideas.plainDefinition: Price signals are market prices treated as condensed information about scarcity, demand, supply, and tradeoffs.
ideas.context: In the Hayek path, prices help people coordinate without one person knowing the whole economy.
ideas.whyMatters: Price signals matter because the market argument is not only greed. It is also an information argument.

sources.title: Hayek / The Use of Knowledge in Society

ideas.title: Market Coordination
ideas.plainDefinition: Market coordination means buyers, sellers, prices, competition, and exchange organize activity without one central plan.
ideas.context: In the Hayek path, market coordination is defended as a way to use local knowledge.
ideas.whyMatters: Market coordination matters because the road needs to compare actual mechanisms, not slogans.
